did_you_know.text: The tribes of Gad and Reuben asked for the land east of the Jordan because they had large herds, and they saw that the lands of Jazer and Gilead were especially suitable for raising sheep and cattle.
The tribes of Gad and Reuben asked to receive the land east of the Jordan as their inheritance and even proposed not crossing with the rest of the people into the land west of the Jordan.
Moses feared that the two tribes’ decision to stay behind would weaken the people’s morale, so he asked, “Shall your brothers go to war while you sit here?”
Moses recalled the spies and pointed out that Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh were the only ones of that generation who followed the Lord wholeheartedly and entered the land.
The tribes of Gad and Reuben pledged to build towns for their families and enclosures for their flocks, while their fighting men would go ahead of the Israelites.

The tribes emphasized that they would not return to their homes until all the Israelites had received their inheritance, even though their own inheritance had already been assigned east of the Jordan.

Moses established that the promise was not merely a social commitment but also a religious obligation: if they failed to keep it, they would sin against the Lord, and they should know that their sin would find them out.

The inheritance east of the Jordan was given not only to the tribes of Gad and Reuben but also to half the tribe of Manasseh; it included the kingdoms of Sihon king of the Amorites and Og king of Bashan.
The tribes of Gad and Reuben built fortified cities and enclosures for their flocks, and they built or rebuilt towns including Dibon, Ataroth, Jazer, Heshbon, and Nebo.

The families of Manasseh also took part in conquering the land east of the Jordan: the descendants of Machir captured Gilead, Jair captured their settlements, and Nobah captured Kenath and its surrounding villages.
